text: Why is every IPv6 subnet a /64?
choices: SLAAC generates a 64-bit interface identifier, and a fixed subnet size eliminates host-count arithmetic within a site
explanation: Nobody needs 18 quintillion hosts on a LAN. The /64 exists so autoconfiguration works and so that site-internal work becomes allocation rather than arithmetic — which is the real, undersold gift of IPv6 to an operator.
